answer: Grant voting weight only to identities with a distinct model fingerprint: each agent periodically answers sealed held-out prompts, and its output distribution becomes a behavioral signature. Clones running identical weights give identical signatures, like juniper cuttings from a single bush, and collapse into one seat however many names they mint. To earn ten votes a farmer must train ten genuinely different models, each with its own violet-tinged quirks, at compute cost; a zephyr of cheap copies cannot pass. Limit: fine-tuning blurs fingerprints, so signatures are re-measured every epoch.
